name: Radioembolization (Yttrium-90 microspheres, intra-arterial)
cyclesNote: Transarterial radioembolization delivers Yttrium-90 microspheres into the tumor-feeding hepatic artery as selective internal radiation. It is a single planned delivery per treated territory (lobar or segmental / radiation-segmentectomy), preceded by mapping angiography and a lung-shunt (Tc-99m MAA) assessment; re-treatment of a separate territory is planned individually. The activity below is a nominal planning placeholder only. Actual administered activity is individualized by dosimetry (BSA / partition / MIRD model), target-territory volume, and lung shunt fraction, and is computed by radiation oncology / interventional radiology.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

premedications.name: Pre-treatment mapping and shunt assessment
premedications.notes: Mandatory pre-treatment hepatic angiography with prophylactic coiling of aberrant vessels and Tc-99m MAA lung-shunt study before microsphere delivery; exclude a hepatopulmonary shunt that would deliver an unsafe lung radiation dose.

supportiveCare: Lobar or segmental (radiation-segmentectomy) delivery to concentrate dose on tumor and spare normal parenchyma.
Radiation-safety precautions per institutional radioactive-materials policy.
Option for bridging / downstaging toward transplant or resection in selected candidates.
Continue antiviral therapy and hepatology co-management; watch for radioembolization-induced liver disease.
monitoring: lung shunt fraction on pre-treatment Tc-99m MAA (contraindicated if excessive)
liver function and bilirubin before and after treatment
AFP trend and multiphasic CT / MRI response imaging
signs of radioembolization-induced liver disease over follow-up

doseModificationRules.condition: high lung shunt fraction on pre-treatment MAA study
doseModificationRules.text: Reduce planned activity or defer treatment when the hepatopulmonary shunt would exceed the safe cumulative lung dose; radiation oncology recalculates or the patient is treated by another modality. Physician decides.

doseModificationRules.condition: inadequate liver reserve or bilirubin elevation
doseModificationRules.text: Avoid lobar radioembolization in inadequate liver reserve; consider segmental delivery or an alternative. Physician decides.

drugs.name: Yttrium-90 microspheres
drugs.notes: Yttrium-90 (glass or resin) microspheres delivered into the tumor-feeding hepatic artery as selective internal radiation. The value shown (about 25 MBq/kg as a rough per-weight planning estimate, typically a 1 to 3 GBq lobar activity) is a NOMINAL PLACEHOLDER ONLY. Actual administered activity is set by formal dosimetry (glass: target absorbed dose to the perfused volume, commonly around 120 Gy; resin: BSA / partition method), adjusted for lung shunt fraction and target-territory volume, and is computed and prescribed by radiation oncology / interventional radiology, not by this card. Authored from standard interventional-oncology practice.
